questions.question: A linear program $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ (slacks included) has a basis $\mathcal{B}$ with basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$. Which coefficients and right-hand side do the constraint rows of the simplex tableau of $\mathcal{B}$ contain?

In the simplex tableau of a basis $\mathcal{B}$, the objective row is $-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}+\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}$. Why is its entry in the column of the $k$-th basic variable $x_{B_k}$ equal to $0$ for every basis?
options: Basic variables have objective coefficient $0$, so both terms of the entry vanish.
Its column of $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}$ is $\boldsymbol{e}_k$, so $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{e}_k=c_{B_k}$ cancels $-c_{B_k}$.
The entry is $0$ only once the tableau is optimal, when all basic entries have been cleared.
Its column of $\boldsymbol{A}$ is $\boldsymbol{e}_k$, so multiplying by $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ leaves it unchanged.

questions.question: For a basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, what does the right-hand side $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$ of the objective row of its tableau represent?
options: The optimal value of the linear program, whichever basis is used.
The sum of the values of the basic variables at the basic solution.
The amount by which $Z$ can still increase from the current basic solution.
The objective value $Z$ at the basic solution of $\mathcal{B}$.

questions.question: The basic variables of a basis $\mathcal{B}$ are listed in the order $(x_4,x_1,x_2)$, and the tableau is then recomputed with the order $(x_1,x_2,x_4)$. How does the new tableau differ from the old one?
options: Only the order of the constraint rows changes; the objective row and the basic solution stay the same.
The objective row changes, because the costs in $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}$ are now listed in a new order.
The columns of $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ are permuted, so the slack columns of the tableau change order.
The basic solution changes, because row $k$ now gives the value of a different variable.

questions.question: A linear program $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ has two $\leq$ constraints with right-hand side $\boldsymbol{b}=(8,6)^{\top}$ and slack variables $x_3,x_4$. The tableau of a basis has right-hand sides $3$ and $4$ in its constraint rows and objective-row entries $2$ and $1$ under $x_3$ and $x_4$. What is the right-hand side of its objective row?

For $\max Z=2x_1+5x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq8$, $x_2\leq4$, $x_1+2x_2\leq11$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $x_3,x_4,x_5$, the basis ordered $(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}=(3,4,1)^{\top}$. What is the right-hand side of the objective row of its tableau?

The constraints $3x_1+2x_2+x_3+x_4=10$ and $x_1+x_2+2x_3+x_5=4$ (slacks $x_4,x_5$) have the basis ordered $(x_1,x_2)$ with $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&-2\\-1&3\end{bmatrix}$. What is the coefficient of $x_3$ in the tableau row of the basic variable $x_2$?

For $\max Z=4x_1+3x_2+5x_3$ subject to two $\leq$ constraints with slack variables $x_4,x_5$, the tableau of the basis ordered $(x_2,x_1)$ has the column $(2,-1)^{\top}$ under the nonbasic $x_3$ in its constraint rows. What is the reduced cost $\bar{c}_3$, the objective-row entry of $x_3$?

For $\max Z=3x_1-2x_2+5x_3$ subject to two $\leq$ constraints with slacks $x_4,x_5$ and $\boldsymbol{b}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, take the slack basis $(x_4,x_5)$, so $\boldsymbol{B}=\boldsymbol{I}_2$ and $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}=\boldsymbol{0}$. Which entries does the objective row of its tableau have under $x_1,x_2,x_3$?

A basis $\mathcal{B}$ of a linear program in equation form $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}=(3,-2)^{\top}$. Which statement about the simplex tableau of $\mathcal{B}$ is correct?
options: It is not defined, since the formula may only be applied to a basis with $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$.
It is defined, but $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$ is then not the objective value of its basic solution.
It is defined, and the entry $-2$ shows that the linear program has no feasible solution.
It is defined as usual; its right-hand side shows a basic solution that is not feasible, with $x_{B_2}=-2$.

questions.question: A linear program in equation form $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, has the basis ordered $(x_4,x_1,x_2)$. In its simplex tableau the nonbasic $x_5$ has the column $(2,0,-1)^{\top}$ in the constraint rows. Which relation between the columns of $\boldsymbol{A}$ follows?
In the simplex tableau of a basis $\mathcal{B}$, the right-hand side of the second constraint row is $b'_2=0$. Which statement about the second basic variable $x_{B_2}$ is correct?
options: It stays basic with value $0$; its column is still $\boldsymbol{e}_2$ and its objective-row entry is $0$.
It counts as nonbasic because its value is $0$, so its column need not be a unit vector.
It stays basic, but its objective-row entry becomes $-c_{B_2}$ because it adds nothing to $Z$.
The tableau is not valid for $\mathcal{B}$, since every basic variable must have a positive value.

questions.question: For $\max Z=2x_1+3x_2+4x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+2x_3\leq6$, $x_1+2x_2+x_3\leq8$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $x_4,x_5$, the basis ordered $(x_1,x_2)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}$. What is the reduced cost $\bar{c}_3$, the objective-row entry of $x_3$ in its tableau?

In the tableau of a basis ordered $(x_1,x_5)$, the nonbasic $x_3$ has column entries $a'_{13}=2$, $a'_{23}=-1$, and $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}=(6,3)^{\top}$. If $x_3$ is raised from $0$ to $2$, other nonbasic variables stay $0$ and $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ is kept, what are $x_1$ and $x_5$?

In a simplex tableau of a linear program with constraints $x_1+2x_2+4x_3+x_4=5$ and $x_1+3x_2+x_3+x_5=7$ (slacks $x_4,x_5$), the columns under $x_4$ and $x_5$ form the matrix $\begin{bmatrix}3&-2\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}$. Which column does $x_3$ have in the constraint rows of this tableau?

Starting from the slack basis, two students carry out different sequences of Gauss-Jordan pivots, and both end with the basic variables $(x_2,x_1,x_5)$ in that row order. How are their two final tables related?
options: They are identical, since every entry is fixed by $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ and the data $\boldsymbol{A}$, $\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{c}$.
Their right-hand sides agree, but nonbasic columns may differ, as they depend on the pivots made.
They are identical only if the basis is optimal; earlier tables depend on the pivot path taken.
Their constraint rows agree, but objective rows may differ, as each pivot adds other row multiples.

questions.question: The initial system $Z-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=0$, $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ has augmented block matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1&-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}&0\\\boldsymbol{0}&\boldsymbol{A}&\boldsymbol{b}\end{bmatrix}$. Which block matrix, multiplied on the left, turns it into the simplex tableau of a basis with basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$?

A linear program in equation form has only the variables $x_1,\dots,x_4$. The constraint rows of the tableau of the basis $(x_1,x_2)$ read $x_1+3x_3+x_4=7$ and $x_2+2x_3+x_4=4$. What are the values of $x_3$ and $x_4$ in the basic solution of the basis $(x_3,x_4)$?

Constraints $x_1+3x_2+x_3=9$ and $2x_1+x_2-x_4=8$ have a slack $x_3$ and a surplus variable $x_4$, all variables $\geq0$. The basis ordered $(x_1,x_2)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}-\frac{1}{5}&\frac{3}{5}\\\frac{2}{5}&-\frac{1}{5}\end{bmatrix}$. Which column does $x_4$ have in the constraint rows of the tableau?
